newsitem.title: UK: Berlusconi denied final appeal in UK papers case.
newsitem.headline: Berlusconi denied final appeal in UK papers case.

text.p: Lawyers representing Italian business tycoon Silvio Berlusconi on Wednesday were denied an appeal to England's highest court, the House of Lords, in their attempt to stop the transfer of papers to Italy.

The papers, subject of drawn out legal arguments over the past six months, were seized in April by Britain's Serious Fraud Office at the request of Italian authorities investigating allegations of fraud and false accounting.

In a High Court hearing last Friday, Lord Justice Simon Brown said he did not believe the appellants -- Berlusconi, his company Fininvest and company president Fedele Confalonieri -- had grounds for any further appeals.
A source at the Serious Fraud Office said there was now no reason for the transfer of the papers to be further delayed.

Brown had rejected an appeal against the transfer of the documents which he said were linked to fraud and false accounting allegations amounting to 51 million pounds ($82.72 million) which had been "surreptitiously removed from Fininvest and used for criminal purposes."
Berlusconi, who leads the centre-right opposition, is a former Italian prime minister and has extensive business holdings which include TV channels and the football club AC Milan. ($1=.6165 Pound)
